name: West Virginia

agency.name: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection, Office of Oil and Gas (OOG)

form.name: Well Work Permit Application: WW-6B for horizontal (section 22-6A) wells, WW-2B for all other wells
form.notes: Read WW-6B (3 pages, 25 items) and WW-2B (13 items, in the 2016 non-6A packet), plus in the 43-page horizontal 6A packet: the checklist, WW-9 fluids and cuttings plan, WW-6A1 lease information, WW-6A notice and the site safety plan outline (BOP, H2S, directional survey). Not read: plat WW-6, GPS form WW-7, water management plan, fee schedule page, WR-35 completion report, operator registration OP-1. Horizontal 6A applications need a long packet (notices, plat, safety plan, water plan, bond, fee); the forms index says the packet was last revised 2016 and WW-6B 04-15-2015, so newer versions may exist online only. Filing is on paper or document upload (Application Enhancer), not confirmed.

api_number.n: API Number 10 and 14 digit in the weekly report; api in the layer

permit_number.n: Layer permitid (county code, dash, 5-digit sequence); same as the API tail; weekly report gives API only

well_name.n: Weekly 'Well Number' and layer wellnumber (operator's well number); WW-6B item 2

lease_name.n: Layer farmname (WW-6B item 3 'Farm Name/Surface Owner'); weekly report has none

operator_name.n: Operator in the weekly report; respparty in the layer; some may be individuals

operator_id.n: WW-6B and WW-2B item 1 'Operator ID'; WW-9 'OP Code'; not in the weekly report or layer

operator_type.n: Not on WW-6B or WW-2B; Operator Registration (OP-1) not read

bond.n: H6A checklist: $250,000 bond; bond forms OP-7, OP-8; not on WW-6B; not in the data

county.n: County Name in the weekly report; 3-digit county code in the layer

district.n: WW-6B/2B 'District' is the county magisterial district, not an agency region; code list exists

field_pool.n: WW-6B and WW-2B ask target formations, not a field or pool name

surface_latlon.n: Layer WellX and WellY (datum not checked); plat WW-6 and GPS form WW-7 not read

surface_plss.n: Not PLSS; forms give quadrangle and district; plat WW-6 (footages?) not read

bottom_hole_loc.n: End of the 'Horizontal laterals (simplified)' line layer; no BH field; WW-6B has leg length only

lateral_path.n: 'Horizontal laterals (simplified)' polyline layer; accuracy not checked; site safety plan has survey items

elevation.n: WW-6B item 4: current ground and proposed post-construction; WW-2B item 3; not in the data

surface_owner.n: WW-6B item 3 and WW-6A notice list surface owners; layer farmname may be the same item (unchecked)

well_type.n: Weekly 'Well Type'; layer welltype and welluse (e.g. Gas Production); WW-6B item 5

work_type.n: Weekly 'Permit Type' (New Drill, Plugging...) and 'Permit_Action'; layer permittype

well_direction.n: Weekly Well Type: Vertical, Horizontal, Horizontal 6A; layer welltype

proposed_depth_md.n: WW-6B item 10 total measured depth; layer welldepth is only a class ('Shallow greater than 3,000 feet')

proposed_depth_tvd.n: WW-6B item 8 proposed total vertical depth; WW-2B item 6 'Proposed Total Depth'

lateral_length.n: WW-6B item 11 proposed horizontal leg length

target_formation.n: WW-6B item 7; layer 'formation' read NA on a new permit, so not relied on

formation_tops.n: WW-6B item 7 depths and thickness; items 12-16 fresh water, salt water, coal, void depths

casing_program.n: WW-6B item 18 casing and tubing program, packers; WW-2B item 13

cement_program.n: WW-6B item 18 fill-up, cement type and yield; item 24 additives

pressure_control.n: Site Safety Plan outline item 5 BOP and well control; required for H6A and deep wells only

h2s.n: Site Safety Plan outline item 6 hydrogen sulfide; H6A and deep wells only

pit_waste.n: WW-9: pit use and waste, liner, disposal method, closed loop, cuttings disposal, reclamation

water.n: WW-9 asks if over 5,000 bbl of water; Water Management Plan form (H6A) not read

fracture_plan.n: WW-6B item 20 methods, max pressure and rate; frac additive list with CAS numbers (H6A checklist)

frac_dates.n: WR-35 asks dates frac activities began and ceased, and a date per stage; the data layer holds only compdate

frac_chemicals.n: Copy of the FracFocus disclosure must be attached to the WR-35 (35 CSR 8, 10.1.a); no chemical data published

frac_additives.n: List of additives actually used is required with the completion report (22-6A-7(e)(5)); none published as data

frac_amounts.n: WR-35 gives proppant, water and nitrogen per stage; ingredient amounts only in the attached FracFocus copy

spacing_unit.n: No unit or acreage item on WW-6B or WW-2B (acres disturbed only)

spacing_exception.n: WW-6A7 well restriction checklist: setbacks with surface-owner waiver or DEP variance (H6A)

mineral_owner.n: WW-6A1 lease information: lessor, lessee, royalty, book and page; WW-6A notice to coal owner

fee.n: H6A checklist (rev 2013): $10,150 first well, $5,150 next; Fee Schedule page not read

notice_hearing.n: WW-6A notice to owners and water purveyors, WW-PN publication notice, WW-6AC certification

date_received.n: Layer recdate (yyyy/mm/dd text), e.g. a month before the issue date

date_approved.n: Layer issuedate (exact day); weekly report gives only the week (file name)

date_expires.n: No expiry on WW-6B or in the data; validity rule not read

spud_date.n: Layer has no spud field; a 2010 third-party note says WV publishes none; WR-35 not read

completion_date.n: Layer compdate (empty on a new permit); weekly report lists WR-35_approved actions

status.n: Layer wellstatus (e.g. Permit Issued); weekly Permit_Action: Issued, Modification, Cancelled

plat_image.n: Signed, sealed plat (WW-6) required; documents sit in a login-gated system, not opened

form_image.n: Permits and documents are in Application Enhancer, which asks for a login; not opened

completion_report.n: WR-35 is the completion record; weekly page says completion reports are posted; not opened

logs.n: Not seen on any page or file opened

production_link.n: Annual production Excel files by year, quarterly H6A files and a well search; files not opened

sources.name: WVDEP oil and gas MapServer, layer 7 'All DEP Wells' (one row per well with the latest permit's type and dates; also layers for horizontal wells, active, other status, coal bed methane, plugged, brine disposal, horizontal laterals and well pads)
sources.license: none stated; agency disclaimer on accuracy
sources.tested: Service JSON answered 200 (5 KB; Map, Query, Data; 3,000 records a page; description says data come from RBDMS, adopted August 2016). Layer 7 schema read (25 fields, dates are yyyy/mm/dd text). Four small queries answered 200: one well by API; a count by permit type over the whole layer (154,247 rows, 40 permit types: 29,730 Plugging, 3,611 New Drill, 1,595 Re-Work, 1,804 UIC Permit); and counts for two weeks that match the weekly reports (week of 2026-10-19: 1 New Drill, 20 Plugging = the 21 Issued rows; week of 2019-01-07: 9 New Drill, 3 Plugging, 1 Drilling Deeper against 10, 3 and 1 Issued in the weekly file, with Modification and Cancelled rows absent). Dates run to 2026-10-29 for Plugging, so it is fresher than the weekly zip.

sources.name: Search for Oil and Gas Wells (web search with an issue-date filter, permit type and operator) and Application Enhancer (documents including newly issued permits, plats and forms)
sources.tested: Not requested (the layer above holds the same permit fields). Named in the agency's pages and in search results; the weekly page says Application Enhancer needs a user name and password that the page itself prints (shared, public); not used because it is a login system and bulk files exist.

grade_reason: Two free bulk sources reachable from here without login: the weekly permit reports (a real list of each week's permit actions since 2019: API, action Issued or Modification or Cancelled or WR-35_approved, permit type, well type, operator, county) and the TAGIS map service (one row per well with exact issue date and received date, permit type, well type, status, coordinates, 154,247 rows). Counts of one week matched in both. Two weaknesses: the weekly list has no date column (only the week in the file name), and the layer keeps only each well's latest permit, so older new-drill permits can drop out (2019 week: 9 of 10) and modifications are missing.
producer_plan: Use both. (1) Recent and exact: query the MapServer layer 7 with where issuedate between the first and last day of the month and group by permittype (and welltype); paginate with resultOffset (3,000 per page); dates are yyyy/mm/dd text so string comparison works; no geometry needed. New Drill = new; Re-Drill and Partial Plug Re-drill = reentry; Re-Work, Drilling Deeper, Fracture = recomplete; UIC Permit, Convert, Brine Disposal, Secondary Recovery Well = injection; Plugging, Partial Plug, Storage, General Permit, Emergency Permit and older labels = other. (2) Complete action counts since 2019: download each Weekly Permit Report zip from the archive folders (one zip per week, name 'Weekly Permit Report MM-DD-YYYY'), read the xlsx (stdlib zip and XML), keep rows by Permit_Action: Issued = permits issued, Modification = amend, Cancelled = withdrawn, WR-35_approved = completion approvals; map Permit Type as above. Put a week in the month of its Monday, or split it by the layer's issue dates. Caveats: the layer shows only the latest permit per well, so use it for the last year or two and the weekly files for history; the weekly zip appears a few days after the week ends (week of 10-19 posted 10-27); a Modification repeats a well already counted; horizontal 6A wells are only a few a week while plugging permits dominate (20 of 22 in the sample week), so filter Permit Type. One request every few seconds, one host at a time.
privacy_notes: The weekly list and the layer name operators (a few may be individuals) and the layer's farm name is the form's 'Farm Name/Surface Owner' item, which can be a landowner's surname; the forms collect owner and neighbor names and addresses, which are not published in the data. Publish only entity operators, county and counts; do not publish farm names. The Application Enhancer login is not to be used.
